newsitem.title: USA: Flooded N. Dakota city cancels fireworks.
newsitem.headline: Flooded N. Dakota city cancels fireworks.

text.p: Flood-ravaged Grand Forks cancelled its Fourth of July fireworks show Thursday as steady rain pushed the Red River out of its banks and made the site too dangerous to hold a celebration.
A civic group, the Sertoma Club, said it would hold its annual party later this summer.

The river's expected crest of 30 feet was only two feet above flood stage and about 25 feet short of the record level reached during the massive April flood but it will create a fast current and make the bank too slippery for spectators.

The Red River overtopped dikes and flooded this city 11 weeks ago, forcing nearly the entire population of 50,000 to flee their homes. A fire then destroyed several downtown blocks, which remain largely uninhabited.

Demolition crews began knocking down 125 condemned structures in two hard-hit neighbourhoods this week and city zoning administrator Tim Mann said more damaged homes will likely fall to the bulldozer.

A recent poll taken to gauge the mood of the equally devastated town of East Grand Forks, Minnesota, which had a population of 8,500 before the flood, found at least 85 percent of residents planned to stay. That figure encouraged city officials, who feared losing 20 percent of the town's population.
